cues.en: So you've asked yourself again, who's it for?
cues.zh: 你再次問自己：這是給誰看的？

cues.en: And you've answered your own question.
cues.zh: 也回答了自己的問題。

cues.en: And it's the people you're working with, the ones you're sitting next to, or maybe they're in a a group chat.
cues.zh: 對象是和你一起工作的人，坐在你旁邊的人，或者群組聊天室裡的人。

cues.en: And now, in today's day and age, it saddens me how many communication channels there are, because most of them encourage communicating too often.
cues.zh: 在這個時代，溝通管道多得讓我有些難過，因為多數管道都鼓勵大家溝通得太頻繁。

cues.en: Now, one thing you'll probably pick up is that unless it's an emergency, now is often never the best time.
cues.zh: 你大概會逐漸發現，除非是緊急狀況，否則「現在」往往不是最好的溝通時機。

cues.en: So let's break this down.
cues.zh: 我們來拆開看。

cues.en: Projects you work on will have arbitrarily long timelines with many milestones, plans and steps.
cues.zh: 你參與的專案，時程可能很長，包含許多里程碑、計畫和步驟。

cues.en: And keep in mind, the longer the timescale, the worse humans are at dealing with them.
cues.zh: 記住，時間跨度越長，人類就越不擅長處理。

cues.en: Break it down.
cues.zh: 把它拆小。

cues.en: Days and weeks are much easier.
cues.zh: 「天」和「週」是更容易

cues.en: Units of time to understand.
cues.zh: 理解的時間單位。

cues.en: What are you working on this week?
cues.zh: 這週你要做什麼？

cues.en: Write it down.
cues.zh: 把它寫下來。

cues.en: Share it with the team.
cues.zh: 分享給團隊。

cues.en: This not only consolidates your thinking.
cues.zh: 這不只能整理你的思緒，

cues.en: It gives your team an opportunity to ask questions and offer advice.
cues.zh: 也讓團隊有機會提問、提供建議。

cues.en: You'll find that short term progress often disappoints, but long term progress surprises.
cues.zh: 你會發現，短期進度往往令人失望，長期進展卻常讓人驚喜。

cues.en: So if you're working on a six month project, you can break this down, like starting from zero months.
cues.zh: 所以，如果你在做一個為期六個月的專案，就可以把它拆開，從第零個月開始。

cues.en: It might be hard to realize what's happening right at the end.
cues.zh: 一開始可能很難想像最後會發生什麼。

cues.en: So you break it down.
cues.zh: 所以把它拆小。

cues.en: You've got a four week month.
cues.zh: 一個月有四週。

cues.en: You break one month into four weeks and then you break one week into five days.
cues.zh: 把一個月拆成四週，再把一週拆成五天。

cues.en: I don't know about you, but when I try to think of something that's six months ahead, I have a lot of trouble.
cues.zh: 不知道你如何，但我要思考六個月後的事，就會覺得很困難。

cues.en: But when I break it down to go, what can I do today?
cues.zh: 可是，若把它拆開，問自己今天能做什麼，

cues.en: That's going to add up to this week and what can I do in this month that's going to add up to this first month here and then go same for the next one.
cues.zh: 讓今天的成果累積成這一週的進度；這個月又能做什麼，累積成第一個月的成果，下一個月也照做，

cues.en: Same for the third one.
cues.zh: 第三個月也一樣。

cues.en: And then by the time I get to this end of six months, I realize, wow, I've actually come a long way and it's all from breaking it down into days and weeks.
cues.zh: 等六個月結束時，就會發現，哇，我真的走了很遠，而這全是因為把事情拆成天和週。

cues.en: Now, the first part of this is what did you work on today?
cues.zh: 第一部分就是：今天做了什麼？

cues.en: Now, of course, this is just one technique that you might want to try, but you could set a reminder for the end of each day and have it ask you, what did you work on today?
cues.zh: 當然，這只是你可以嘗試的一種技巧。你可以設定每天結束時的提醒，問自己今天做了什麼。

cues.en: Your response doesn't have to be too long, but it should be written down.
cues.zh: 回答不用太長，但應該寫下來。

cues.en: You could use the following template what I worked on today.
cues.zh: 你可以用這個範本：今天做的事情。

cues.en: So 1 to 3 points on what you did.
cues.zh: 用一到三個重點說明你做了什麼。

cues.en: Maybe you could do what's working, what's not working, what could be improved, and what I'm working on next.
cues.zh: 也可以寫哪些事情順利、哪些不順利、哪些可以改善，以及接下來要做什麼。

cues.en: What's your next course of action based on the above and why?
cues.zh: 根據前面的內容，下一步行動是什麼？為什麼？

cues.en: What's holding you back?
cues.zh: 是什麼阻礙了你？

cues.en: Remember that conversation want to have with your project manager or team lead or something like that?
cues.zh: 記得剛才說，要和專案經理、團隊負責人之類的人談這些事嗎？

cues.en: They want to be able to remove roadblocks for you so you can get back to doing the work you're best at to coding projects.
cues.zh: 他們希望能替你排除阻礙，讓你回去做最擅長的工作，也就是撰寫程式、進行專案。

cues.en: Relate all of these back to the overall project goal.
cues.zh: 把這些內容都連回專案的整體目標。

cues.en: That's six month project.
cues.zh: 就是那個六個月的專案。

cues.en: Pretty hard to understand in one go, but day by day, week by week, sending these updates through to your team, this is really going to help out.
cues.zh: 一次掌握整個專案很難，但每天、每週把這些更新傳給團隊，會很有幫助。

cues.en: And so what you want to do is take note of the overlaps which questions arise.
cues.zh: 接著，留意重複出現的地方，以及大家提出哪些問題。

cues.en: If a question gets asked more than three times, it should be documented somewhere for others to reference.
cues.zh: 如果同一個問題被問了超過三次，就應該記錄在某個地方，供其他人查閱。

cues.en: And you'll see that some of the communication points for the people you're sitting with cross over with your project manager, just like we've discussed before.
cues.zh: 你會發現，和身邊同事溝通的部分重點，也適用於專案經理，正如剛才討論過的。

cues.en: Now, of course, I trust your smart enough to figure out when the things that you're communicating with your teammates also need to be communicated with your project managers and seniors.
cues.zh: 當然，我相信你夠聰明，能判斷哪些和隊友溝通的事情，也需要告訴專案經理或資深成員。

cues.en: It's going to be hard to put in any of these communication techniques with people on your team if you don't actually have a job or aren't on a team yet.
cues.zh: 如果你還沒有工作，或還沒加入團隊，就很難實際運用這些團隊溝通技巧。

cues.en: So in the next video, we'll look at what to do before you have a job.
cues.zh: 所以下一支影片，我們來看看還沒有工作時可以怎麼做。
